# Emberfall Fund — Rapid Grants Application

**Applicant:** Morgan Hale (individual)  
**Project:** Halcyon Threshold — Independent AI Safety Evaluation Microgrants  
**Requested Amount:** $15,000  
**Duration:** 6 months  
**Contact:** morgan@halcyonthreshold.org

---

## 1. What we'll do

Run a lightweight microgrants program making 6–10 grants of $1,500–$3,000 each to independent researchers doing concrete AI safety evaluation work. Focus areas:

- Capability evaluations (measuring what models can do)
- Interpretability evaluations (measuring how well we understand model internals)
- Red-teaming / adversarial evaluations (finding failure modes)
- Evaluation methodology / benchmark development

Grants will be awarded on a rolling basis with a simple two-page application: what you're evaluating, why it matters, what you need, and a one-paragraph budget. Decisions within two weeks.

Recipients must publish results (or a substantive postmortem) within 90 days. We'll aggregate findings into a public landscape document.

---

## 2. Why this is neglected

- Major funders (Open Philanthropy, LTFF, SFF) typically make grants ≥$25k with months-long cycles — too slow and too large for a researcher who needs $2k for compute credits to run an eval suite on a new model.
- Labs' own eval programs (OpenAI Evals, Anthropic's) understandably prioritize their own models and research agendas.
- Independent evals often happen on Discord, in blog posts, or not at all — no lightweight funding exists to professionalize them.
- A microgrants program run by someone embedded in the independent researcher community (me) can move faster and evaluate proposals on technical merit rather than institutional affiliation.

---

## 3. Why me

- I've spent the last six months attending AI safety meetups, talking to independent researchers, and mapping who's doing what. I know the people, the gaps, and the friction points.
- I have technical background (Python, ML basics) sufficient to evaluate eval proposals for feasibility.
- I'm not affiliated with a lab or large org — no COI, no bureaucracy.
- Halcyon Threshold is set up as a vehicle for this kind of work: lean, public-facing, mission-aligned.

---

## 4. Budget ($15,000 total)

| Item | Amount |
|------|--------|
| Microgrants (6–10 grants @ $1,500–$3,000) | $12,000 |
| Compute credits for recipients (AWS/GCP/Azure via my account) | $2,000 |
| Administrative (transaction fees, Notion/Airtable for tracking) | $500 |
| Publication of landscape document (design, hosting) | $500 |

---

## 5. Accountability

- I (Morgan Hale) am the named applicant and will be personally accountable for all funds.
- All grants, decisions, and outcomes will be published transparently on halcyonthreshold.org.
- Emberfall Fund will receive a brief mid-point update (3 months) and final report (6 months) with grant list, outcomes, and lessons learned.
- If Halcyon Threshold incorporates during the grant period, the grant transfers to the entity; otherwise it remains with me personally.

---

## 6. Timeline

- **Weeks 1–2:** Launch application, promote through independent researcher networks (Alignment Forum, Discord, meetups, newsletters)
- **Weeks 3–20:** Rolling review and disbursement
- **Weeks 20–26:** Recipients complete work, publish results
- **Week 26:** Publish aggregated landscape document, final report to Emberfall

---

## 7. Risks & mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|------------|
| Too few quality applications | Promote widely; if needed, proactively reach out to known independent eval researchers |
| Recipients don't deliver | Small grant sizes limit downside; require brief monthly check-ins; publish postmortems even for failed attempts |
| My employment situation changes | Grant is personal, not tied to employer; work happens evenings/weekends regardless |
| Legal/tax complications for unincorporated entity | Grants are gifts to individuals for research; consult Emberfall on compliance; incorporate if needed |

---

## 8. What success looks like

- 8+ independent eval projects funded that wouldn't have happened otherwise
- At least 5 public writeups / benchmark results / eval tools released
- A landscape document cited by other funders and researchers
- Proof that a $15k microgrants program can surface neglected work — enabling a larger follow-on round
